functions.description: Sets the maximum allocated size (capacity) of the buffer to size bytes, potentially shrinking or reserving capacity. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error. Exact behavior on shrink/expand is not documented here.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.
size is a size in bytes; further constraints are unknown.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferEmpty
functions.description: Removes all data from the buffer, making it empty. Capacity may be retained; exact behavior is not documented.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferSwap
functions.description: Swaps the internal state (data, size, capacity, alloc mode) of two buffers.
requirements: buf1 and buf2 must be non-NULL pointers to initialized or created xmlSecBuffer instances.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferAppend
functions.signature: int xmlSecBufferAppend(xmlSecBufferPtr buf, const xmlSecByte* data, xmlSecSize size);
functions.description: Appends size bytes from data to the end of the buffer, reallocating as needed. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.
data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory; data may be NULL only if size is 0 (typical pattern; exact rule not documented).
Caller must check return value and handle negative values as errors.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferPrepend
functions.signature: int xmlSecBufferPrepend(xmlSecBufferPtr buf, const xmlSecByte* data, xmlSecSize size);
functions.description: Prepends size bytes from data to the beginning of the buffer, reallocating as needed. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.
data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory; data may be NULL only if size is 0 (typical pattern; exact rule not documented).
Caller must check return value and handle negative values as errors.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferRemoveHead
functions.description: Removes size bytes from the beginning (head) of the buffer, shifting remaining data as needed. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.
size must be less than or equal to the current buffer size to succeed; behavior on larger values is likely an error (inferred from function purpose).
Caller must check return value for errors.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferRemoveTail
functions.description: Removes size bytes from the end (tail) of the buffer. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.
size must be less than or equal to the current buffer size to succeed; behavior on larger values is likely an error (inferred from function purpose).
Caller must check return value for errors.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferReverse
functions.description: Reverses the order of bytes in the buffer's data. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.
Operation applies to the current logical size of the buffer; exact details are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferReadFile
functions.signature: int xmlSecBufferReadFile(xmlSecBufferPtr buf, const char* filename);
functions.description: Reads the contents of a file specified by filename into the buffer. Whether it replaces existing data or appends is not documented here. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.
filename must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated path to a readable file.
Caller must handle I/O errors via the negative return value.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferBase64NodeContentRead
functions.description: Reads a Base64-encoded text content from the given XML node and stores the decoded bytes into the buffer. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.
node must be a valid libxml2 xmlNodePtr whose content is Base64-encoded; exact accepted formats/whitespace handling are not documented.
Caller must check for negative return values as errors.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferBase64NodeContentWrite
functions.signature: int xmlSecBufferBase64NodeContentWrite(xmlSecBufferPtr buf, xmlNodePtr node, int columns);
functions.description: Encodes the buffer's data as Base64 and writes it into the given XML node's content. The columns parameter likely controls line wrapping; exact semantics are not documented here. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.
node must be a valid libxml2 xmlNodePtr that can accept content modification.
columns is an integer; exact valid range/behavior is unknown.
Caller must check for negative return values as errors.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferHexRead
functions.signature: int xmlSecBufferHexRead(xmlSecBufferPtr buf, const xmlChar* hexStr);
functions.description: Parses a hexadecimal string and stores the resulting bytes into the buffer. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer.
hexStr must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string representing hex data; accepted formats (whitespace, case, prefix) are not documented.
Caller must check for negative return values as errors.

functions.name: xmlSecBufferCreateOutputBuffer
functions.description: Creates and returns a libxml2 xmlOutputBuffer that writes its output into the provided xmlSecBuffer. Useful for streaming APIs that expect an xmlOutputBuffer. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized or created xmlSecBuffer that remains valid for the lifetime of the created xmlOutputBuffer.
Caller is responsible for closing/freeing the returned xmlOutputBuffer via the appropriate libxml2 API; exact function to use is not documented here.
On failure, returns NULL; caller must check before use.

functions.name: xmlSecNodeSetCreate
functions.signature: xmlSecNodeSetPtr xmlSecNodeSetCreate(xmlDocPtr doc, xmlNodeSetPtr nodes, xmlSecNodeSetType type);
functions.description: Creates a new enhanced node set (xmlSecNodeSet) for the given XML document and initial node set, with the specified node-set interpretation type. Typically used to build a working selection of nodes for XML security processing (e.g., transforms, signatures). Ownership/retention of doc and nodes is not specified in this header; the function returns a new xmlSecNodeSet that references them.
requirements: doc should be a valid pointer to an xmlDoc representing the document that owns the nodes (inferred from parameters and struct).
nodes may be NULL or a valid xmlNodeSetPtr produced by libxml2 XPath routines (inferred).
type must be a valid xmlSecNodeSetType enum value.

functions.name: xmlSecNodeSetDestroy
functions.description: Destroys an xmlSecNodeSet and releases its internal resources. If the node set is configured to destroy the document (destroyDoc flag set), the associated xmlDoc will also be destroyed. Use when the node set is no longer needed.
requirements: nset must be a valid pointer previously obtained from xmlSecNodeSetCreate or related xmlsec factory functions.
After this call, nset must not be used again.
If the node set was configured to destroy its document, the caller must not free the xmlDoc separately (inferred from struct field destroyDoc).

functions.name: xmlSecNodeSetDocDestroy
functions.description: Marks or adjusts the node set so that its associated xmlDoc will be destroyed when the node set is destroyed. Intended to transfer document lifetime management to the node set.
requirements: nset must be a valid xmlSecNodeSet pointer.
After calling this, destroying the node set will also destroy its associated xmlDoc; the caller should not free the xmlDoc separately (inferred from name and struct field destroyDoc).

functions.name: xmlSecNodeSetContains
functions.signature: int xmlSecNodeSetContains(xmlSecNodeSetPtr nset, xmlNodePtr node, xmlNodePtr parent);
functions.description: Checks whether the given node (and optionally its parent) is included in the effective node set as defined by nset->type and potential combinations. Returns an integer status (0/1 or negative on error depending on implementation) indicating membership.
requirements: nset must be a valid xmlSecNodeSet pointer.
node should be a valid xmlNodePtr from the same xmlDoc as nset->doc (inferred).
parent may be NULL or a valid parent of node; if provided, it should correspond to node's actual parent (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSecNodeSetAdd
functions.signature: xmlSecNodeSetPtr xmlSecNodeSetAdd(xmlSecNodeSetPtr nset, xmlSecNodeSetPtr newNSet, xmlSecNodeSetOp op);
functions.description: Combines two node sets using the specified operation (intersection, subtraction, or union) and returns the resulting node set (often by linking/augmenting nset). Used to build composite selections across sets.
requirements: nset may be NULL (to start a new set) or a valid xmlSecNodeSet pointer (inferred from common pattern).
newNSet must be a valid xmlSecNodeSet pointer to add/combine.
op must be a valid xmlSecNodeSetOp (xmlSecNodeSetIntersection, xmlSecNodeSetSubtraction, or xmlSecNodeSetUnion).
All node sets involved should refer to nodes from compatible/related documents (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSecNodeSetAddList
functions.signature: xmlSecNodeSetPtr xmlSecNodeSetAddList(xmlSecNodeSetPtr nset, xmlSecNodeSetPtr newNSet, xmlSecNodeSetOp op);
functions.description: Adds a node set to a list-form node set, combining according to the operation and organizing children under the list semantics (xmlSecNodeSetList). Returns the updated or resulting node set.
requirements: nset may be NULL or a valid xmlSecNodeSet pointer. If acting as a list container, its type should be xmlSecNodeSetList (inferred from struct comment).
newNSet must be a valid xmlSecNodeSet pointer.
op must be a valid xmlSecNodeSetOp value.
All node sets involved should be compatible in terms of document ownership (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSecNodeSetGetChildren
functions.signature: xmlSecNodeSetPtr xmlSecNodeSetGetChildren(xmlDocPtr doc, const xmlNodePtr parent, int withComments, int invert);
functions.description: Creates a node set representing the children of the given parent node, optionally including comment nodes and optionally inverting the selection (i.e., selecting all document nodes except those children). Useful for defining canonicalization or transform scopes.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDocPtr for the document containing parent.
parent must be a valid pointer to a node within doc.
withComments should be 0 or 1 to indicate whether comment nodes are included (inferred from name and struct enum patterns).
invert should be 0 or 1 to control selection inversion (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSecNodeSetWalk
functions.signature: int xmlSecNodeSetWalk(xmlSecNodeSetPtr nset, xmlSecNodeSetWalkCallback walkFunc, void* data);
functions.description: Iterates over nodes in the node set and invokes the provided callback once per node. The callback can signal an error/stop by returning a negative value. Returns 0 on success or a negative value if an error occurs or the walk is interrupted per the callback contract.
requirements: nset must be a valid xmlSecNodeSet pointer.
walkFunc must be a valid function pointer matching xmlSecNodeSetWalkCallback signature.
The callback should return 0 on success for each node or a negative value to indicate an error and request interruption (per typedef comment).
data is an opaque pointer passed to each callback invocation and may be NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecNodeSetDumpTextNodes
functions.description: Writes or dumps the text nodes contained in the node set to the given libxml2 output buffer. Useful for serialization or debugging text content. Returns an integer status (0 on success, negative on error in typical xmlsec/libxml2 style).
requirements: nset must be a valid xmlSecNodeSet pointer.
out must be a valid xmlOutputBufferPtr opened for writing; its lifetime/closure is managed by the caller (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSecNodeSetDebugDump
functions.description: Prints a human-readable debug dump of the node set to the given FILE stream (e.g., stdout or stderr), including structure and possibly node information. Intended for diagnostics.
requirements: nset must be a valid xmlSecNodeSet pointer.
output must be a valid FILE* opened for writing; passing stdout or stderr is typical (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListSetDefaultAllocMode
functions.description: Sets the library-wide default memory allocation mode and initial capacity used for xmlSecPtrList instances. Intended to influence how lists grow/allocate by default. Exact effects and thread-safety semantics are not documented here.
requirements: defAllocMode must be a valid xmlSecAllocMode value.
defInitialSize is an initial capacity hint; concrete range/semantics are not documented in this header.
May affect subsequently created/initialized lists; exact timing and thread-safety guarantees are unknown.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListInitialize
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecPtrListInitialize(xmlSecPtrListPtr list, xmlSecPtrListId id);
functions.description: Initializes a pre-allocated xmlSecPtrList structure with the specified item klass (id). Use this when managing the list object’s lifetime externally (stack/embedded).
requirements: list must be non-NULL.
id should be a valid xmlSecPtrListId (klass) describing the list items; lists are considered valid when list != NULL and list->id != NULL.
The list must not be previously initialized; call xmlSecPtrListFinalize before re-initializing.
Check the returned status code to detect initialization failure (exact success/failure codes are not documented here).

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListFinalize
functions.description: Finalizes a previously initialized xmlSecPtrList, releasing internal resources and items per the klass’ destroyItem method.
requirements: list must be a valid, previously initialized xmlSecPtrList.
After finalization, the list must not be used unless re-initialized.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListCreate
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new xmlSecPtrList configured with the given item klass (id).
requirements: id should be a valid xmlSecPtrListId (klass).
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL to detect allocation/initialization failure.
The returned list must be destroyed with xmlSecPtrListDestroy.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListDestroy
functions.description: Destroys a list created by xmlSecPtrListCreate (or initialized list whose ownership is transferred), releasing all resources and items via the klass’ destroyItem.
requirements: list may be NULL-safe or not; this header does not specify. Prefer passing a valid pointer or checking before calling.
After destruction, the pointer must not be used.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListEmpty
functions.description: Removes all items from the list, destroying them via the klass’ destroyItem, but keeps the list object allocated for reuse.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListCopy
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecPtrListCopy(xmlSecPtrListPtr dst, xmlSecPtrListPtr src);
functions.description: Copies items from src to dst, typically duplicating items using the klass’ duplicateItem method (deep copy semantics implied by naming).
requirements: dst must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList compatible with src’s klass.
src must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList.
Behavior regarding existing items in dst is not specified here; callers should assume dst may be modified or cleared.
Caller must check the returned status code; exact numeric conventions are not documented here.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListDuplicate
functions.description: Creates a new list that is a duplicate of the given list, likely copying items via the klass’ duplicateItem method.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect allocation/copy failure.
The returned list must be destroyed with xmlSecPtrListDestroy.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListGetSize
functions.description: Returns the current number of items in the list.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListGetItem
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlSecPtr xmlSecPtrListGetItem(xmlSecPtrListPtr list, xmlSecSize pos);
functions.description: Returns the item pointer at the given index position.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList.
pos must refer to an existing element index within the list’s current size (0-based).
Return value may be NULL on invalid position or if the stored item itself is NULL; this header does not specify which, so callers must handle NULL safely.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListAdd
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecPtrListAdd(xmlSecPtrListPtr list, xmlSecPtr item);
functions.description: Appends an item pointer to the end of the list.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList.
item must be suitable for the list’s klass; nullability acceptance is not specified here.
Caller must check the returned status code; exact success/failure codes are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListInsert
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecPtrListInsert(xmlSecPtrListPtr list, xmlSecPtr item, xmlSecSize pos);
functions.description: Inserts an item pointer at the specified position, shifting subsequent items forward.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList.
pos must be within valid insertion bounds (typically 0..current_size).
item must be suitable for the list’s klass; acceptance of NULL is not specified.
Caller must check the returned status code; exact codes are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListSet
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecPtrListSet(xmlSecPtrListPtr list, xmlSecPtr item, xmlSecSize pos);
functions.description: Replaces the item at the specified position with the provided item pointer.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList.
pos must refer to an existing element index (0-based).
If an item is already present at pos, it may be destroyed via the klass’ destroyItem; exact behavior is not specified here.
Caller must check the returned status code; exact codes are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListRemove
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecPtrListRemove(xmlSecPtrListPtr list, xmlSecSize pos);
functions.description: Removes the item at the specified position from the list, typically destroying it via the klass’ destroyItem.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList.
pos must refer to an existing element index (0-based).
Caller must check the returned status code; exact codes are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListRemoveAndReturn
functions.description: Removes and returns the item at the specified position without destroying it, transferring ownership to the caller.
requirements: list must be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList.
pos must refer to an existing element index (0-based).
Caller must handle a possible NULL return (out-of-range or allocation/other error unspecified).
The caller becomes responsible for the returned item’s lifetime.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListDebugDump
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT void xmlSecPtrListDebugDump(xmlSecPtrListPtr list, FILE* output);
functions.description: Prints a human-readable debug dump of the list and its items to the given FILE stream.
requirements: list should be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList (may print nothing if NULL; behavior not specified).
output must be a valid, writable FILE* stream.

functions.name: xmlSecPtrListDebugXmlDump
functions.description: Prints an XML-formatted debug dump of the list and its items to the given FILE stream.
requirements: list should be a valid, initialized xmlSecPtrList (may print nothing if NULL; behavior not specified).
output must be a valid, writable FILE* stream.

functions.name: xmlSecStringListGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the xmlSecPtrList klass descriptor for lists of strings (xmlChar*), suitable for use as the id when creating or initializing string lists.
requirements: Caller should use the returned klass with xmlSecPtrListCreate or xmlSecPtrListInitialize.
No arguments; always check for NULL if robustness is required.

functions.name: xmlSecBnCreate
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new big number (xmlSecBn) buffer with an initial capacity of size bytes. Use when you need a standalone big number object managed by the xmlsec library.
requirements: size may be zero or positive; exact constraints are not documented
Returns NULL on allocation failure; callers must check the result
The returned object must be released with xmlSecBnDestroy

functions.name: xmlSecBnDestroy
functions.description: Destroys and frees a big number created with xmlSecBnCreate, releasing all associated resources.

functions.name: xmlSecBnInitialize
functions.description: Initializes a pre-allocated xmlSecBn (xmlSecBuffer) structure for use as a big number with an initial capacity of size bytes. Use for stack- or embedded-allocated structs instead of xmlSecBnCreate.
requirements: bn must be a valid, allocated xmlSecBn structure
bn must not already be initialized
size may be zero or positive; exact constraints are not documented

functions.name: xmlSecBnFinalize
functions.description: Finalizes an initialized xmlSecBn, releasing internal resources. Use for objects initialized by xmlSecBnInitialize.
requirements: bn must have been successfully initialized with xmlSecBnInitialize

functions.name: xmlSecBnGetData
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal byte buffer storing the big number in binary form.
requirements: bn must be a valid, initialized or created xmlSecBn
Returned pointer may become invalid after subsequent bn modifications; do not hold it across calls that may reallocate the buffer
The buffer may be NULL if bn is empty; exact semantics are not documented
Do not write beyond the current size reported by xmlSecBnGetSize

functions.name: xmlSecBnSetData
functions.signature: int xmlSecBnSetData(xmlSecBnPtr bn, const xmlSecByte* data, xmlSecSize size);
functions.description: Replaces the big number value with the provided binary data of length size bytes.
requirements: bn must be a valid, initialized or created xmlSecBn
If size > 0, data must be a valid pointer to at least size bytes
If size == 0, data may be NULL (exact allowance not documented)
Returns a status code; exact success/error conventions are not documented (caller must check and handle non-success values)

functions.name: xmlSecBnGetSize
functions.description: Returns the current size in bytes of the big number’s internal buffer (the value length).
requirements: bn must be a valid, initialized or created xmlSecBn

functions.name: xmlSecBnZero
functions.description: Sets the big number value to zero (clears its content).
requirements: bn must be a valid, initialized or created xmlSecBn

functions.name: xmlSecBnFromString

functions.description: Parses a numeric string in the specified base and stores the resulting value into bn as binary data.

str must be a NUL-terminated string in the given base; exact allowed characters and bases are not documented
base specifies the numeric base; valid range is not documented

functions.name: xmlSecBnToString
functions.description: Converts the big number value into a NUL-terminated string representation in the specified base and returns a newly allocated xmlChar string.
requirements: bn must be a valid, initialized or created xmlSecBn
base specifies the numeric base; valid range is not documented

str must be a NUL-terminated hex string; case-sensitivity and prefix handling are not documented
Returns a status code; caller must check for failure

functions.name: xmlSecBnToHexString
functions.description: Converts the big number value into a hexadecimal NUL-terminated string and returns a newly allocated xmlChar string.
requirements: bn must be a valid, initialized or created xmlSecBn
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check
The returned string must be freed by the caller using the appropriate deallocator (typically xmlFree), exact allocator not stated

functions.name: xmlSecBnFromDecString
functions.signature: int xmlSecBnFromDecString(xmlSecBnPtr bn, const xmlChar* str);

Returns a status code; caller must check for failure

functions.name: xmlSecBnToDecString
functions.description: Converts the big number value into a decimal NUL-terminated string and returns a newly allocated xmlChar string.
requirements: bn must be a valid, initialized or created xmlSecBn
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check

functions.name: xmlSecBnMul

functions.name: xmlSecBnDiv

functions.name: xmlSecBnAdd

requirements: bn must be a valid, initialized or created xmlSecBn
Behavior for negative delta is not documented
Returns a status code; caller must check for failure

functions.name: xmlSecBnReverse

functions.name: xmlSecBase64CtxCreate
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a Base64 context for streaming encode or decode, depending on encode. Use with Update/Final functions to process data in chunks.
requirements: encode selects mode: non-zero for encode, zero for decode (inferred from name and typical patterns; exact accepted values not documented).
columns is the maximum encoded line length when in encode mode; constraints not specified here.
On success returns a non-NULL context pointer; returns NULL on allocation/initialization failure (common C pattern; specific error codes not documented).
The returned context must be released with xmlSecBase64CtxDestroy.

functions.name: xmlSecBase64CtxDestroy
functions.description: Releases and cleans up a Base64 context previously created with xmlSecBase64CtxCreate.
requirements: ctx must be a context obtained from xmlSecBase64CtxCreate (or successfully initialized via xmlSecBase64CtxInitialize) and not already destroyed/finalized by this function.
Do not use ctx after this call.
Behavior for NULL ctx is not specified; pass a valid pointer.

functions.name: xmlSecBase64CtxInitialize
functions.signature: int xmlSecBase64CtxInitialize(xmlSecBase64CtxPtr ctx, int encode, int columns);
functions.description: Initializes a caller-provided Base64 context structure for streaming encode or decode (depending on encode). Use when managing the context’s memory yourself.
requirements: ctx must point to allocated storage for a xmlSecBase64Ctx and must not already be initialized.
encode selects mode: non-zero for encode, zero for decode (inferred; exact accepted values not documented).
columns is the maximum encoded line length in encode mode; constraints not specified here.
On success returns a non-negative/zero status (exact convention not documented); on failure returns an error code (unspecified).
A successfully initialized context must later be finalized with xmlSecBase64CtxFinalize (and the storage freed by the caller if allocated manually).

functions.name: xmlSecBase64CtxFinalize
functions.description: Finalizes a Base64 context initialized with xmlSecBase64CtxInitialize, releasing internal resources. Does not free the memory of the ctx object itself.
requirements: ctx must have been successfully initialized with xmlSecBase64CtxInitialize.
Call this once per successful initialization before freeing or reusing the storage.
Do not use the context for Update/Final after finalization unless re-initialized.

functions.name: xmlSecBase64CtxUpdate_ex
functions.signature: int xmlSecBase64CtxUpdate_ex(xmlSecBase64CtxPtr ctx, const xmlSecByte* in, xmlSecSize inSize, xmlSecByte* out, xmlSecSize outSize, xmlSecSize* outWritten);
functions.description: Feeds a chunk of input into the Base64 context and produces encoded/decoded output. Use repeatedly to process streaming data. Writes up to outSize bytes into out and optionally reports the number of bytes written via outWritten.
requirements: ctx must be a valid Base64 context initialized for the desired mode (encode or decode) using xmlSecBase64CtxCreate or xmlSecBase64CtxInitialize.
in may be NULL only if inSize is 0; otherwise must point to at least inSize bytes of readable memory (inferred from common API patterns).
out must point to a buffer of size at least outSize bytes if outSize > 0; buffer must be writable.
outWritten may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the number of bytes actually written.
The function can be called multiple times; preserve ctx between calls without modifying it directly.
Ensure outSize is large enough for worst-case output for the given mode and input size to avoid truncation; exact sizing rules are not documented here.
Return value is an integer status code; exact success/error conventions are not specified in this header.

functions.name: xmlSecBase64CtxFinal_ex
functions.signature: int xmlSecBase64CtxFinal_ex(xmlSecBase64CtxPtr ctx, xmlSecByte* out, xmlSecSize outSize, xmlSecSize* outWritten);
functions.description: Finishes the Base64 streaming operation, flushing any buffered state and writing remaining output to out. Call after the last Update_ex to obtain any final bytes.
requirements: ctx must be a valid Base64 context that has been initialized and (optionally) used with xmlSecBase64CtxUpdate_ex.
out must point to a buffer of size at least outSize bytes if outSize > 0; buffer must be writable.
outWritten may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the number of bytes actually written.
Call exactly once per streaming operation after all Update_ex calls and before destroying/finalizing the context.
Return value is an integer status code; exact success/error conventions are not specified in this header.

functions.name: xmlSecBase64Encode
functions.signature: xmlChar* xmlSecBase64Encode(const xmlSecByte* in, xmlSecSize inSize, int columns);
functions.description: Encodes a memory buffer to Base64 and returns a newly allocated, null-terminated xmlChar string containing the encoded data. columns controls line wrapping of the output.
requirements: in may be NULL only if inSize is 0; otherwise must point to at least inSize bytes of readable memory.
columns is the desired maximum line length; exact valid range and special values are not documented here. Use XMLSEC_BASE64_LINESIZE for the library default.
Returns a pointer to an allocated xmlChar string on success; on failure returns NULL (typical pattern; exact conditions not documented).
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned string using the appropriate allocator for this library; the exact deallocation function is not specified in this header.

functions.name: xmlSecBase64Decode_ex
functions.signature: int xmlSecBase64Decode_ex(const xmlChar* str, xmlSecByte* out, xmlSecSize outSize, xmlSecSize* outWritten);
functions.description: Decodes a Base64-encoded, null-terminated string str into binary data, writing up to outSize bytes into out and optionally reporting the number of bytes written via outWritten.
requirements: str must be a null-terminated xmlChar string containing Base64 data; it must be readable for the length of the string.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least outSize bytes if outSize > 0.
outWritten may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the number of bytes actually written.
Ensure outSize is sufficient for the decoded output to avoid truncation; exact sizing rules are not documented here.
Return value is an integer status code; exact success/error conventions are not specified in this header.

functions.name: xmlSecBase64DecodeInPlace
functions.description: Decodes a Base64-encoded, null-terminated string in place, writing the resulting binary data back into the same buffer and optionally reporting the number of bytes written. The resulting data will not be a null-terminated string.
requirements: str must be a mutable buffer containing a null-terminated Base64 string; it must be writable, as the decoded bytes will overwrite the input.
The buffer backing str must be large enough to hold the input (it is overwritten with fewer bytes during decode).
outWritten may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the number of bytes written (decoded length).
After decoding, the contents are binary and may include zero bytes; do not treat str as a C string unless you manage termination separately.
Return value is an integer status code; exact success/error conventions are not specified in this header.

functions.name: xmlSecGetDefaultLineFeed
functions.description: Returns the current library-wide default line feed sequence used by xmlsec when generating or formatting XML text. The returned pointer is read-only and expected to remain valid for the lifetime of the process.
requirements: No arguments required.
The returned pointer is const; callers must not modify or free it.

functions.name: xmlSecSetDefaultLineFeed
functions.description: Sets the library-wide default line feed sequence used when producing XML text. Intended to control newline style globally (e.g., "\n" vs "\r\n").
requirements: If provided, linefeed should point to a valid null-terminated string.
Global setting; calling this affects subsequent operations that consult the default line feed.
Thread-safety/ordering guarantees are not documented; callers should avoid concurrent changes.

functions.name: xmlSecGetNodeNsHref
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT const xmlChar* xmlSecGetNodeNsHref(const xmlNodePtr cur);
functions.description: Returns the namespace URI (href) associated with the given node, or NULL if none. Useful for QName comparisons and filtering.
requirements: cur must be a valid xmlNodePtr (element) or NULL.
The returned pointer is owned by libxml2 and must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: xmlSecGetNodeContentAndTrim
functions.description: Returns the textual content of a node with leading/trailing whitespace trimmed. Typically aggregates text from the node’s children per libxml2 semantics.
requirements: cur must be a valid xmlNodePtr or NULL.
On success, returns a newly allocated xmlChar*; caller is responsible for freeing it with xmlFree.
May return NULL on error or if no content is available.

functions.name: xmlSecGetNodeContentAsSize
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecGetNodeContentAsSize(const xmlNodePtr cur, xmlSecSize defValue, xmlSecSize* res);
functions.description: Parses a node’s textual content as an unsigned size (xmlSecSize). If content is absent or invalid, a default value may be used.
requirements: res must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result.
cur must be a valid node if content is expected; behavior when cur is NULL is unspecified.
defValue is used when content is missing/invalid (exact rules are not documented).
Return value conventions are not documented here; callers should check for non-zero/negative as failure per xmlsec patterns.

functions.name: xmlSecCheckNodeName
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecCheckNodeName(const xmlNodePtr cur, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns);
functions.description: Checks whether the node matches the specified local name and namespace URI. Intended for fast QName equality tests.
requirements: cur must be a valid xmlNodePtr (typically an element).
name should be a non-NULL local name for deterministic comparison.
ns should be the namespace URI (href) for deterministic comparison; passing NULL semantics are not documented.
Return value semantics (1/0 vs 0/-1) are not documented; treat non-zero as match per common practice.

functions.name: xmlSecGetNextElementNode
functions.description: Skips non-element nodes and returns the next sibling that is an element node, or NULL if none.
requirements: cur may be NULL; otherwise must be a valid node pointer.
Returned node is owned by the document; do not free.

functions.name: xmlSecFindSibling
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlNodePtr xmlSecFindSibling(const xmlNodePtr cur, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns);
functions.description: Searches sibling elements of cur and returns the first element whose local name and namespace URI match the given values.
requirements: cur must be a valid node pointer.
name should be the target local name; ns should be the namespace URI (href).
Returned node is borrowed from the document; do not free.
Behavior when name or ns are NULL is not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecFindChild
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlNodePtr xmlSecFindChild(const xmlNodePtr parent, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns);
functions.description: Finds the first child element of parent matching the given local name and namespace URI.
requirements: parent must be a valid element node pointer.
name should be non-NULL local name; ns should be the namespace URI (href).
Returned node is owned by the document; do not free.

functions.name: xmlSecFindParent
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlNodePtr xmlSecFindParent(const xmlNodePtr cur, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns);
functions.description: Walks up the ancestor chain from cur and returns the first ancestor element that matches the given local name and namespace URI.
requirements: cur must be a valid node pointer.
name and ns should be the expected local name and namespace URI.
Returned node is borrowed from the document; do not free.

functions.name: xmlSecFindNode
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlNodePtr xmlSecFindNode(const xmlNodePtr parent, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns);
functions.description: Searches within the subtree rooted at parent for an element with the specified local name and namespace URI, returning the first match or NULL.
requirements: parent must be a valid node pointer.
name and ns should specify the target QName.
Returned node is owned by the document; do not free.
Exact search order (preorder/DFS/BFS) is not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecAddChild
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlNodePtr xmlSecAddChild(xmlNodePtr parent, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns);
functions.description: Creates a new element with the given local name and namespace URI and appends it as the last child of parent. Returns the newly created node.
requirements: parent must be a valid element node within a document.
name must be a non-NULL, valid local name.
ns may be NULL (namespace handling not explicitly documented).
Parent and created node belong to the same document; when mixing documents, import/adopt per libxml2 conventions.

functions.name: xmlSecEnsureEmptyChild
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlNodePtr xmlSecEnsureEmptyChild(xmlNodePtr parent, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns);
functions.description: Ensures there is exactly one child element under parent with the specified name and namespace and that it has no children/content. Creates it if missing and removes any existing content.
requirements: parent must be a valid element node.
name must be non-NULL; ns may be NULL (exact semantics not documented).
May remove or replace existing children/content of the matched child element.
Returned node is owned by the document; do not free.

functions.name: xmlSecAddChildNode
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlNodePtr xmlSecAddChildNode(xmlNodePtr parent, xmlNodePtr child);
functions.description: Appends an existing node as a child of parent and returns it. Useful for moving nodes within a tree.
requirements: parent and child must be valid xmlNodePtr.
Parent and child should belong to the same xmlDoc; otherwise import/adopt per libxml2 before calling.
After insertion, child is owned by the parent/document; caller must not free it directly.

functions.name: xmlSecAddNextSibling
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlNodePtr xmlSecAddNextSibling(xmlNodePtr node, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns);
functions.description: Creates a new element with the given name and namespace and inserts it as the next sibling of node. Returns the new node.
requirements: node must be a valid xmlNodePtr attached to a document.
name must be non-NULL local name; ns may be NULL (not documented).
New node must be created in the same document as node.

functions.name: xmlSecAddPrevSibling
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlNodePtr xmlSecAddPrevSibling(xmlNodePtr node, const xmlChar *name, const xmlChar *ns);
functions.description: Creates a new element with the given name and namespace and inserts it as the previous sibling of node. Returns the new node.
requirements: node must be a valid xmlNodePtr attached to a document.
name must be non-NULL local name; ns may be NULL (not documented).
New node must be created in the same document as node.

functions.name: xmlSecReplaceNode
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecReplaceNode(xmlNodePtr node, xmlNodePtr newNode);
functions.description: Replaces node in the tree with newNode. Intended to swap an element in-place.
requirements: node and newNode must be valid xmlNodePtr.
Both nodes should belong to the same document; import/adopt if necessary.
After replacement, ownership of old node’s position is taken by newNode; the old node may be detached (exact disposal semantics not documented).
Return value semantics are not documented; check for non-zero/negative as failure per xmlsec conventions.

functions.name: xmlSecReplaceNodeAndReturn
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecReplaceNodeAndReturn(xmlNodePtr node, xmlNodePtr newNode, xmlNodePtr* replaced);
functions.description: Replaces node with newNode and returns the replaced node via the replaced out-parameter for further processing or cleanup.
requirements: node and newNode must be valid.
replaced must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the replaced node.
Nodes should be from the same document.
Return code conventions are not documented; check for failure per xmlsec patterns.

functions.name: xmlSecReplaceContent
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecReplaceContent(xmlNodePtr node, xmlNodePtr newNode);
functions.description: Replaces the children/content of node with newNode (commonly used to set the content subtree).
requirements: node must be a valid container element.
newNode must be a valid node (typically a subtree root).
Both nodes should be in the same document; import as needed.
Existing children/content of node may be removed.
Return code semantics are not documented here.

functions.name: xmlSecReplaceContentAndReturn
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecReplaceContentAndReturn(xmlNodePtr node, xmlNodePtr newNode, xmlNodePtr* replaced);
functions.description: Replaces the content (children) of node with newNode and returns the replaced content node via replaced.
requirements: node and newNode must be valid.
replaced must be a non-NULL pointer for the removed content node(s); exact structure is not documented.
Nodes should belong to the same document.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecReplaceNodeBuffer
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecReplaceNodeBuffer(xmlNodePtr node, const xmlSecByte *buffer, xmlSecSize size);
functions.description: Replaces the content of node with text constructed from the given byte buffer of length size. Useful for setting textual content from binary data after encoding as needed.
requirements: node must be a valid element or text container.
If size > 0, buffer must be non-NULL.
Assumes proper encoding/escaping is handled by the function; exact encoding is not documented.
Return value semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecReplaceNodeBufferAndReturn
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecReplaceNodeBufferAndReturn(xmlNodePtr node, const xmlSecByte *buffer, xmlSecSize size, xmlNodePtr* replaced);
functions.description: Replaces the content of node with text from buffer and returns the previous content node via replaced.
requirements: node must be valid.
If size > 0, buffer must be non-NULL.
replaced must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the previous content node.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecNodeEncodeAndSetContent
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecNodeEncodeAndSetContent(xmlNodePtr node, const xmlChar *buffer);
functions.description: Encodes special XML characters in buffer and sets the result as the node’s textual content.
requirements: node must be a valid xmlNodePtr.
buffer may be NULL or a valid null-terminated xmlChar string (exact NULL handling not documented).
Caller does not need to pre-escape content; the function performs necessary encoding.
Return value semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecAddIDs
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT void xmlSecAddIDs(xmlDocPtr doc, xmlNodePtr cur, const xmlChar** ids);
functions.description: Registers attributes listed in ids as type ID within the document, starting at the subtree rooted at cur. Enables ID-based lookups by libxml2/xmlsec.
requirements: doc must be a valid xmlDocPtr.
cur must be a valid node pointer within doc.
ids should be a list/array of attribute local names; termination and format are not documented here (commonly a NULL-terminated array).
Affects DTD/ID handling in the document.

functions.name: xmlSecCreateTree
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlDocPtr xmlSecCreateTree(const xmlChar* rootNodeName, const xmlChar* rootNodeNs);
functions.description: Creates a new XML document with a single root element of the given local name and namespace URI and returns the document.
requirements: rootNodeName must be a non-NULL valid local name.
rootNodeNs may be NULL (namespace behavior not documented).
On success returns a new document that the caller owns; free it with xmlFreeDoc.

functions.name: xmlSecIsEmptyNode
functions.description: Checks whether the node is considered empty (no element children and possibly no significant text). Returns non-zero if empty, zero otherwise.
requirements: node must be a valid xmlNodePtr.
Exact emptiness criteria (e.g., whitespace-only text) are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecIsEmptyString
functions.description: Checks whether the string is empty or possibly NULL. Returns non-zero if considered empty, zero otherwise.
requirements: str may be NULL or a valid null-terminated xmlChar string.
Exact definition of "empty" (e.g., whitespace-only) is not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecGetQName
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlChar* xmlSecGetQName(xmlNodePtr node, const xmlChar* href, const xmlChar* local);
functions.description: Builds and returns a QName (with prefix if needed) string for the given local name and namespace URI in the context of node, creating or reusing a prefix mapping as appropriate.
requirements: node must be a valid node within a document with namespace context.
local must be a non-NULL local name.
href may be NULL to indicate no namespace or default namespace (exact behavior not documented).
Returns a newly allocated xmlChar*; caller must free with xmlFree.
May return NULL on failure.

functions.name: xmlSecPrintXmlString
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecPrintXmlString(FILE * fd, const xmlChar * str);
functions.description: Prints the given UTF-8 XML string to the provided FILE stream, handling necessary escaping/encoding as implemented by xmlsec.
requirements: fd must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
str may be NULL or a valid null-terminated xmlChar string (exact NULL handling not documented).
Return value semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2IntegerGetInfo
functions.description: Looks up and returns a pointer to the mapping entry in the QName-to-Integer table that matches intValue.
requirements: info must point to a valid, statically defined table of xmlSecQName2IntegerInfo entries; termination criteria are not documented (commonly a sentinel entry).
Returned pointer is to table data; do not free.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2IntegerGetInteger
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecQName2IntegerGetInteger(xmlSecQName2IntegerInfoConstPtr info, const xmlChar* qnameHref, const xmlChar* qnameLocalPart, int* intValue);
functions.description: Resolves a QName (href + local part) via the provided mapping table into its corresponding integer value and stores it in intValue.
requirements: info must be a valid mapping table.
qnameHref and qnameLocalPart should be non-NULL and refer to the target QName.
intValue must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2IntegerGetIntegerFromString
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecQName2IntegerGetIntegerFromString(xmlSecQName2IntegerInfoConstPtr info, xmlNodePtr node, const xmlChar* qname, int* intValue);
functions.description: Parses a QName string (potentially with prefix) in the namespace context of node, resolves it to href+local, and maps it via the table to an integer stored in intValue.
requirements: info must be a valid mapping table.
node must be a valid node providing namespace context.
qname must be a non-NULL QName string.
intValue must be non-NULL to receive the integer value.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2IntegerGetStringFromInteger
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlChar* xmlSecQName2IntegerGetStringFromInteger(xmlSecQName2IntegerInfoConstPtr info, xmlNodePtr node, int intValue);
functions.description: Converts an integer to its corresponding QName and returns a QName string appropriate for the namespace context of node (possibly with a prefix).
requirements: info must be a valid mapping table.
node must be a valid node with namespace context for prefix resolution.
On success, returns a newly allocated xmlChar*; caller must free with xmlFree.
May return NULL if intValue is unknown or on error.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2IntegerNodeRead
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecQName2IntegerNodeRead(xmlSecQName2IntegerInfoConstPtr info, xmlNodePtr node, int* intValue);
functions.description: Reads the textual content of node as a QName (using node’s namespace context), resolves it via the mapping table, and stores the corresponding integer in intValue.
requirements: info must be a valid mapping table.
node must be a valid node whose content holds a QName.
intValue must be non-NULL to receive the result.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2IntegerNodeWrite
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecQName2IntegerNodeWrite(xmlSecQName2IntegerInfoConstPtr info, xmlNodePtr node, const xmlChar* nodeName, const xmlChar* nodeNs, int intValue);
functions.description: Creates or sets a child element under node (or modifies node, depending on implementation) with the given name and namespace, writing the QName corresponding to intValue as its text content.
requirements: info must be valid.
node must be a valid node within a document.
nodeName must be a non-NULL local name; nodeNs may be NULL (exact behavior not documented).
intValue must correspond to a mapping entry; otherwise the function likely fails.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2IntegerAttributeRead
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecQName2IntegerAttributeRead(xmlSecQName2IntegerInfoConstPtr info, xmlNodePtr node, const xmlChar* attrName, int* intValue);
functions.description: Reads a QName from the specified attribute on node, resolves it via the mapping table, and stores the integer value in intValue.
requirements: info must be valid.
node must be a valid element node.
attrName must be a non-NULL attribute local name.
intValue must be non-NULL to receive the result.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2IntegerAttributeWrite
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecQName2IntegerAttributeWrite(xmlSecQName2IntegerInfoConstPtr info, xmlNodePtr node, const xmlChar* attrName, int intValue);
functions.description: Writes the QName corresponding to intValue into the specified attribute on node, creating or updating the attribute as needed.
requirements: info must be valid.
node must be a valid element node.
attrName must be a non-NULL attribute local name.
intValue must correspond to a known mapping; otherwise failure is expected.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2IntegerDebugDump
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT void xmlSecQName2IntegerDebugDump(xmlSecQName2IntegerInfoConstPtr info, int intValue, const xmlChar* name, FILE* output);
functions.description: Writes a human-readable debug representation of the QName<->Integer mapping for intValue to the given FILE stream, labeled by name.
requirements: info must be valid.
output must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
name may be NULL or a label string (exact requirements not documented).

functions.name: xmlSecQName2IntegerDebugXmlDump
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT void xmlSecQName2IntegerDebugXmlDump(xmlSecQName2IntegerInfoConstPtr info, int intValue, const xmlChar* name, FILE* output);
functions.description: Writes an XML-formatted debug dump of the QName<->Integer mapping for intValue to the FILE stream, labeled by name.
requirements: info must be valid.
output must be a valid FILE* for writing.
name may be NULL or a label (not documented).

functions.name: xmlSecQName2BitMaskGetInfo
functions.description: Looks up and returns a pointer to the mapping entry in the QName-to-BitMask table that matches mask (or a single-bit entry within it).
requirements: info must be a valid table of xmlSecQName2BitMaskInfo entries; termination criteria are not documented.
Returned pointer is to table data; do not free.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2BitMaskGetBitMask
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecQName2BitMaskGetBitMask(xmlSecQName2BitMaskInfoConstPtr info, const xmlChar* qnameLocalPart, const xmlChar* qnameHref, xmlSecBitMask* mask);
functions.description: Resolves a QName (local part + href) to its corresponding bitmask value via the mapping table and stores it in mask.
requirements: info must be valid.
qnameLocalPart and qnameHref should be non-NULL for deterministic mapping.
mask must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2BitMaskNodesRead
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecQName2BitMaskNodesRead(xmlSecQName2BitMaskInfoConstPtr info, xmlNodePtr* node, const xmlChar* nodeName, const xmlChar* nodeNs, int stopOnUnknown, xmlSecBitMask* mask);
functions.description: Reads one or more sibling/child nodes with the specified name and namespace starting from *node, accumulates their mapped bitmask values into mask, and advances the node pointer as appropriate. Optionally stops when encountering an unknown QName depending on stopOnUnknown.
requirements: info must be valid.
node must be a non-NULL pointer to an xmlNodePtr; the function may update *node to the position after processed nodes.
nodeName must be a non-NULL local name; nodeNs may be NULL (behavior not documented).
mask must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the accumulated bitmask.
stopOnUnknown controls behavior on unknown entries; exact semantics are not documented.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2BitMaskGetBitMaskFromString
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecQName2BitMaskGetBitMaskFromString(xmlSecQName2BitMaskInfoConstPtr info, xmlNodePtr node, const xmlChar* qname, xmlSecBitMask* mask);
functions.description: Parses a QName string in the namespace context of node, resolves it via the mapping table, and stores the corresponding bitmask in mask.
requirements: info must be valid.
node must be a valid node for namespace resolution.
qname must be a non-NULL QName string.
mask must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2BitMaskGetStringFromBitMask
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT xmlChar* xmlSecQName2BitMaskGetStringFromBitMask(xmlSecQName2BitMaskInfoConstPtr info, xmlNodePtr node, xmlSecBitMask mask);
functions.description: Converts a bitmask value to a QName string appropriate for node’s namespace context and returns it.
requirements: info must be valid.
node must be a valid node with namespace context.
On success, returns a newly allocated xmlChar*; caller must free with xmlFree.
May return NULL if mask cannot be represented or on error.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2BitMaskNodesWrite
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT int xmlSecQName2BitMaskNodesWrite(xmlSecQName2BitMaskInfoConstPtr info, xmlNodePtr node, const xmlChar* nodeName, const xmlChar* nodeNs, xmlSecBitMask mask);
functions.description: Writes one or more child nodes under node with name/nodeNs representing the flags set in mask, using the mapping table to emit appropriate QNames as content or node names (per implementation).
requirements: info must be valid.
node must be a valid node within a document.
nodeName must be a non-NULL local name; nodeNs may be NULL (not documented).
mask is the bitmask to serialize.
Return code semantics are not documented.

functions.name: xmlSecQName2BitMaskDebugDump
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT void xmlSecQName2BitMaskDebugDump(xmlSecQName2BitMaskInfoConstPtr info, xmlSecBitMask mask, const xmlChar* name, FILE* output);
functions.description: Writes a human-readable debug representation of the QName<->BitMask mapping for the given mask to output, labeled by name.
requirements: info must be valid.
output must be a valid FILE* for writing.
name may be NULL or a label (not documented).

functions.name: xmlSecQName2BitMaskDebugXmlDump
functions.signature: XMLSEC_EXPORT void xmlSecQName2BitMaskDebugXmlDump(xmlSecQName2BitMaskInfoConstPtr info, xmlSecBitMask mask, const xmlChar* name, FILE* output);

functions.name: xmlSecTransformMemBufGetKlass

Typical usage is to pass the returned Id to xmlsec transform creation/registration APIs (inferred from xmlsec library patterns).

requirements: transform must be a valid, non-NULL xmlSecTransformPtr (inferred from pointer parameter).
transform must refer to a MemBuf transform instance (i.e., its id should be xmlSecTransformMemBufId) to be usable with this function (inferred from function name and header grouping).
The returned xmlSecBufferPtr, if non-NULL, is owned by the transform; callers must not free or destroy it (inferred from typical getter semantics in xmlsec).
Callers should treat the returned pointer as invalidated once the transform is finalized or destroyed; do not use it after the transform’s lifetime ends (inferred).
Callers should check for a NULL return and handle it as an error or absence of buffer (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSecCryptoDLFunctionsRegisterKeyDataAndTransforms
functions.description: Registers all key data classes and transform implementations exposed by the given crypto dynamic-loading function table with the xmlsec core. Typical usage: obtain or construct an xmlSecCryptoDLFunctions table for a crypto backend (e.g., via xmlSecCryptoDLGetLibraryFunctions or after loading a module) and then call this to make its key data and transforms available to xmlsec. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on failure (xmlsec convention).
requirements: functions must be a valid, initialized pointer to an xmlSecCryptoDLFunctions structure.
Call after the corresponding crypto backend has been loaded or its function table has been fully populated.
Check the integer return value: 0 indicates success; negative value indicates failure.

functions.name: xmlSecCryptoDLInit
functions.description: Initializes the xmlsec crypto dynamic-loading (DL) subsystem. Must be called before using any other xmlSecCryptoDL* functions that load, query, or set crypto backends. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on failure.
requirements: This function should be called before any other dynamic-loading operations in this subsystem.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; negative value indicates failure.
Only available when xmlsec is built with dynamic loading support (XMLSEC_NO_CRYPTO_DYNAMIC_LOADING not defined).

functions.name: xmlSecCryptoDLShutdown
functions.description: Shuts down the xmlsec crypto dynamic-loading subsystem and releases related resources. Call when dynamic-loading operations are no longer needed, typically during library/application shutdown. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on failure.
requirements: Should be called after xmlSecCryptoDLInit and after all dynamic-loading operations are complete.
Do not call other xmlSecCryptoDL* functions that depend on the DL subsystem after shutdown.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; negative value indicates failure.
Only available when xmlsec is built with dynamic loading support (XMLSEC_NO_CRYPTO_DYNAMIC_LOADING not defined).

functions.name: xmlSecCryptoDLLoadLibrary
functions.description: Loads a crypto backend library (plugin/module) identified by the given name and makes its functions available to xmlsec via the DL subsystem. Typical names correspond to supported crypto providers (e.g., "openssl", "gnutls", etc.). Returns 0 on success and a negative value on failure.
requirements: crypto should be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string naming a supported crypto backend.
xmlSecCryptoDLInit must be successfully called before using this function.
The specified backend must be available on the system and compatible with the xmlsec build.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; negative value indicates failure.
Only available when xmlsec is built with dynamic loading support (XMLSEC_NO_CRYPTO_DYNAMIC_LOADING not defined).

functions.name: xmlSecCryptoDLGetLibraryFunctions
functions.description: Returns the function table (xmlSecCryptoDLFunctions) for the specified crypto backend name, if it has been loaded or is otherwise known to the DL subsystem. Use this to access backend-specific registrations or to pass the table to other xmlsec APIs. Returns NULL on error or if the backend is not found.
requirements: crypto should be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string naming a crypto backend.
The named backend must have been loaded/registered prior to this call (e.g., via xmlSecCryptoDLLoadLibrary).
Callers must check for a NULL return pointer to detect errors or missing backends.
Only available when xmlsec is built with dynamic loading support (XMLSEC_NO_CRYPTO_DYNAMIC_LOADING not defined).

functions.name: xmlSecCryptoDLUnloadLibrary
functions.description: Unloads the previously loaded crypto backend identified by the given name and releases its resources from the DL subsystem. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on failure.
requirements: crypto should be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated xmlChar string naming a crypto backend that has been loaded.
Backend should not be in active use by ongoing operations when unloading (inferred common requirement to avoid use-after-free; exact policy not specified).
xmlSecCryptoDLInit must have been called before, and the backend should have been loaded via xmlSecCryptoDLLoadLibrary.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; negative value indicates failure.
Only available when xmlsec is built with dynamic loading support (XMLSEC_NO_CRYPTO_DYNAMIC_LOADING not defined).

functions.name: xmlSecCryptoDLSetFunctions

requirements: functions must be a valid, fully initialized pointer to an xmlSecCryptoDLFunctions structure compatible with the current xmlsec build.
Typically called after loading or constructing a backend’s function table; ensure fields are set before calling.

Only available when xmlsec is built with dynamic loading support (XMLSEC_NO_CRYPTO_DYNAMIC_LOADING not defined).

functions.name: xmlSecCryptoDLGetFunctions

Only available when xmlsec is built with dynamic loading support (XMLSEC_NO_CRYPTO_DYNAMIC_LOADING not defined).

functions.name: xmlSecInit

functions.name: xmlSecCheckVersionExt

Affects only the default callback behavior; has effect if that callback is in use (inferred).

functions.name: xmlSecError

errorObject and errorSubject should be descriptive C strings for the object/subject related to the error; NULL handling is not documented (unknown).
Callers should ensure the function is only used for error reporting and can be invoked from error paths (reentrancy/async-signal-safety not documented; avoid calling from signal handlers).
