functions.description: Returns a pointer to the default password callback function suitable for use with the xmlsec-OpenSSL app key-loading functions. The exact callback type/signature is not declared in this header; treat it as an opaque function pointer compatible with the pwdCallback parameters in the loading APIs.
requirements: Return value must be cast to the appropriate password-callback function type expected by the caller/context.
May be NULL if no default callback is available; callers should handle a NULL result.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509GetKlass
functions.description: Returns the xmlsec key data class (klass) for OpenSSL-backed X509 key data. Use this to register or check that a key data object is of the X509 type for the OpenSSL backend.
requirements: No arguments.
Typically used during initialization/registration or for type checks; caller should not attempt to free the returned klass pointer.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509GetKeyCert
functions.description: Retrieves the primary (key) certificate from an xmlsec OpenSSL X509 key-data container. Intended to access the certificate that corresponds to the key associated with the data.
requirements: data must be non-NULL.
data must be an xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509Id-compatible key data object.
Returned X509* is owned by the key-data container; caller must not free it.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509AdoptKeyCert
functions.description: Sets/adopts the primary (key) certificate into the given OpenSSL X509 key-data container. Ownership of cert is transferred to the container on success.
requirements: data must be non-NULL and must be an xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509Id-compatible object.
cert must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid OpenSSL X509 certificate.
On success, ownership of cert is transferred; caller must not free cert afterwards.
Function returns a status int (0 or positive on success, negative on error per xmlsec conventions). Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509AdoptCert
functions.description: Adds/adopts an additional certificate into the OpenSSL X509 key-data container (not necessarily the key certificate). Ownership of cert is transferred on success.
requirements: data must be non-NULL and must be an xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509Id-compatible object.
cert must be non-NULL and a valid OpenSSL X509 certificate.
On success, ownership of cert is transferred; caller must not free cert afterwards.
Function returns a status int (xmlsec convention: negative on error). Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509GetCert
functions.description: Retrieves the certificate at index pos from the OpenSSL X509 key-data container (enumerating all stored certs).
requirements: data must be non-NULL and must be an xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509Id-compatible object.
pos must be less than the number of certificates stored (see xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509GetCertsSize).
Returned X509* is owned by the container; caller must not free it.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509GetCertsSize
functions.description: Returns the count of certificates stored in the OpenSSL X509 key-data container.
requirements: data must be non-NULL and must be an xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509Id-compatible object.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509AdoptCrl
functions.description: Adds/adopts a CRL into the OpenSSL X509 key-data container. Ownership of crl is transferred on success.
requirements: data must be non-NULL and must be an xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509Id-compatible object.
crl must be non-NULL and a valid OpenSSL X509_CRL object.
On success, ownership of crl is transferred; caller must not free crl afterwards.
Function returns a status int (negative on error). Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509GetCrl
functions.description: Retrieves the CRL at index pos from the OpenSSL X509 key-data container.
requirements: data must be non-NULL and must be an xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509Id-compatible object.
pos must be less than the number of CRLs stored (see xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509GetCrlsSize).
Returned X509_CRL* is owned by the container; caller must not free it.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509GetCrlsSize
functions.description: Returns the count of CRLs stored in the OpenSSL X509 key-data container.
requirements: data must be non-NULL and must be an xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataX509Id-compatible object.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLX509CertGetKey
functions.description: Extracts a key from the given X509 certificate and returns it wrapped as an xmlsec key-data object for use within xmlsec. Typically used to obtain a public key from a certificate. Specifics (key type, ownership) are not fully documented in this header.
requirements: cert must be non-NULL and a valid OpenSSL X509 certificate.
Caller must check for NULL return indicating failure.

Ownership of the returned xmlSecKeyDataPtr is unknown from this header; consult implementation/documentation to determine whether the caller must free it (in xmlsec, created key data usually must be destroyed by the caller).

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataRawX509CertGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the key data class for raw X509 certificate blobs for the OpenSSL backend. Useful for working with raw certificate data within xmlsec.
requirements: No arguments.
Returned klass is managed by the library; caller must not free it.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the key data store class (klass) for the OpenSSL X509 certificate store. Use to create or register an X509 store with xmlsec.
requirements: No arguments.
Returned store klass is owned by the library; caller must not free it.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreVerify
functions.signature: X509* xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreVerify(xmlSecKeyDataStorePtr store, XMLSEC_STACK_OF_X509* certs, XMLSEC_STACK_OF_X509_CRL* crls, xmlSecKeyInfoCtx* keyInfoCtx);
functions.description: Verifies a certificate chain using the given OpenSSL-backed xmlsec X509 store. Optionally uses provided CRLs and verification parameters from keyInfoCtx. Returns a certificate on success (likely the validated certificate); specifics of which certificate is returned are not detailed in this header.
requirements: store must be non-NULL and must be created with xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreGetKlass.
certs must be a non-NULL STACK_OF(X509) containing one or more certificates to verify; order/contents should form a chain suitable for validation.
crls may be NULL or a valid STACK_OF(X509_CRL) to assist revocation checking.
keyInfoCtx must be non-NULL and appropriately initialized for verification settings.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect verification failure/errors.
Ownership of the returned X509*, if any, is not specified here; caller should consult implementation to determine whether it must be freed (often owned by the store or input stack).

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreVerifyKey
functions.signature: int xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreVerifyKey(xmlSecKeyDataStorePtr store, xmlSecKeyPtr key, xmlSecKeyInfoCtxPtr keyInfoCtx);
functions.description: Verifies that the given xmlsec key is valid according to the OpenSSL X509 store and the provided key info context (e.g., checks certificate chain, trust, and constraints).
requirements: store must be non-NULL and created with xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreGetKlass.
key must be non-NULL and initialized; it should contain an X509 certificate/chain compatible with verification.
keyInfoCtx must be non-NULL and initialized with verification parameters.
Returns int status (negative on error per xmlsec conventions). Caller must check return value.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreAdoptCert
functions.signature: int xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreAdoptCert(xmlSecKeyDataStorePtr store, X509* cert, xmlSecKeyDataType type);
functions.description: Adds/adopts an X509 certificate into the OpenSSL xmlsec X509 store with the specified usage/type. Ownership of cert is transferred to the store on success.
requirements: store must be non-NULL and created with xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreGetKlass.
cert must be non-NULL and a valid OpenSSL X509 certificate.
type must be a valid xmlSecKeyDataType flag designating certificate purpose/usage.
On success, ownership of cert is transferred; caller must not free cert.
Returns int status (negative on error). Caller must check return value.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreAdoptCrl
functions.description: Adds/adopts an X509 CRL into the OpenSSL xmlsec X509 store. Ownership of crl is transferred to the store on success.
requirements: store must be non-NULL and created with xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreGetKlass.
crl must be non-NULL and a valid OpenSSL X509_CRL object.
On success, ownership of crl is transferred; caller must not free crl.
Returns int status (negative on error). Caller must check return value.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreAddCertsPath
functions.description: Adds trusted certificates to the OpenSSL xmlsec X509 store from all files in the specified directory path (implementation-dependent format). Useful to load system or bundle trust anchors.
requirements: store must be non-NULL and created with xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreGetKlass.
path must be a non-NULL, valid directory path accessible to the process.
Caller must check return value (negative on error).
The directory contents must contain certificates in a format recognized by the implementation (exact formats not specified here).

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreAddCertsFile
functions.description: Adds trusted certificates to the OpenSSL xmlsec X509 store from the specified file (implementation-dependent format, e.g., PEM bundle).
requirements: store must be non-NULL and created with xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreGetKlass.
filename must be a non-NULL path to a readable certificate file.
Caller must check return value (negative on error).
The file must contain certificates in a format recognized by the implementation (exact formats not specified here).

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreFindCert
functions.signature: XMLSEC_DEPRECATED X509* xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreFindCert(xmlSecKeyDataStorePtr store, xmlChar* subjectName, xmlChar* issuerName, xmlChar* issuerSerial, xmlChar* ski, xmlSecKeyInfoCtx* keyInfoCtx);
functions.description: Deprecated: Searches the OpenSSL xmlsec X509 store for a certificate matching the provided subject/issuer/serial/SKI criteria, using verification context parameters from keyInfoCtx. Prefer newer verification APIs.
requirements: store must be non-NULL and created with xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreGetKlass.
Any of subjectName, issuerName, issuerSerial, ski may be NULL or xmlChar strings describing the match criteria; formats are not documented here.
keyInfoCtx must be non-NULL and initialized.
Caller must check for NULL return indicating not found or error.
Returned X509* ownership is not specified; caller should consult implementation (deprecated function semantics).

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreFindCert_ex
functions.signature: XMLSEC_DEPRECATED X509* xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreFindCert_ex(xmlSecKeyDataStorePtr store, xmlChar* subjectName, xmlChar* issuerName, xmlChar* issuerSerial, xmlSecByte* ski, xmlSecSize skiSize, xmlSecKeyInfoCtx* keyInfoCtx);
functions.description: Deprecated: Extended search for a certificate in the OpenSSL xmlsec X509 store by subject/issuer/serial and binary SKI value of length skiSize, using parameters from keyInfoCtx. Prefer newer verification APIs.
requirements: store must be non-NULL and created with xmlSecOpenSSLX509StoreGetKlass.
subjectName, issuerName, issuerSerial may be NULL or xmlChar strings for matching (formats not specified here).
ski may be NULL or a pointer to SKI bytes; when ski is non-NULL, skiSize must specify the exact length of the SKI buffer.
keyInfoCtx must be non-NULL and initialized.
Caller must check for NULL return indicating not found or error.
Returned X509* ownership is not specified (deprecated function).

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyGetEvp
functions.description: Returns the underlying OpenSSL EVP_PKEY associated with an xmlSecKey. Use when you need to interoperate with OpenSSL APIs using a key managed by xmlsec. The returned pointer is typically a non-owning reference tied to the lifetime of the xmlSecKey.
requirements: key must be a valid, initialized xmlSecKeyPtr created/loaded via xmlsec.
key must contain an OpenSSL-compatible key; otherwise the function may return NULL.
The returned EVP_PKEY pointer must not be freed by the caller unless explicitly documented elsewhere; it is owned by the xmlSecKey.
The returned pointer remains valid only as long as key (and its key data) remains valid.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLEvpKeyDataAdoptEvp
functions.description: Adopts an existing OpenSSL EVP_PKEY into an xmlsec key-data object. After a successful call, the xmlsec key-data owns the EVP_PKEY and will free it when appropriate. Use to import an externally created EVP_PKEY into xmlsec-managed storage.
requirements: data must be a valid, initialized xmlSecKeyDataPtr of an OpenSSL EVP-based key data type (e.g., appropriate for the key algorithm).
pKey must be a valid pointer to an EVP_PKEY allocated/initialized via OpenSSL.
On success, ownership of pKey is transferred to data; the caller must not use or free pKey after success.
On failure (non-zero/negative return), ownership of pKey remains with the caller and must be managed/freed by the caller.
Return value follows xmlsec conventions (commonly 0 on success, a negative value on error); callers must check the return value before assuming adoption succeeded.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLEvpKeyDataGetEvp
functions.description: Retrieves the OpenSSL EVP_PKEY stored inside an xmlsec key-data object. Useful for calling OpenSSL APIs directly with a key managed by xmlsec. The returned pointer is typically owned by the xmlsec key-data.
requirements: data must be a valid, initialized xmlSecKeyDataPtr containing an EVP-based key.
The returned EVP_PKEY pointer may be NULL if data does not hold an EVP_PKEY or on error.
The returned EVP_PKEY is owned by data and must not be freed by the caller.
The pointer remains valid only while data remains valid and unchanged.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLEvpKeyDup
functions.description: Creates and returns a duplicate of the given EVP_PKEY. Use when you need an independent EVP_PKEY that you own and can manage separately from the original.
requirements: pKey must be a valid, initialized EVP_PKEY pointer.
On success, the caller owns the returned EVP_PKEY and must free it with EVP_PKEY_free when no longer needed.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLEvpKeyAdopt
functions.description: Wraps/adopts an existing OpenSSL EVP_PKEY into a new xmlsec key-data object and returns it. After success, xmlsec owns the EVP_PKEY. Use to convert an OpenSSL key into xmlsec-managed key data.
requirements: pKey must be a valid, initialized EVP_PKEY pointer.
On success, ownership of pKey is transferred to the returned xmlSecKeyDataPtr; the caller must not free or use pKey directly after adoption.
On failure (NULL return), ownership of pKey remains with the caller and must be freed/managed by the caller.
The returned xmlSecKeyDataPtr must eventually be released via the appropriate xmlsec key/key-data destruction routines.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataDEREncodedKeyValueGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the xmlsec key-data class (klass) identifier for the OpenSSL-backed DEREncodedKeyValue key data type. Use this when registering, creating, or querying this key-data type within xmlsec.
requirements: No arguments; may return NULL on initialization or configuration errors; callers must check for NULL.
Typically used during xmlsec crypto initialization/registration or when constructing key-data objects of this type.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeysStoreGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the xmlSec key store class identifier for the OpenSSL-backed keys store. Use this id to create or check a key store instance for OpenSSL (e.g., with xmlSecKeyStoreCreate or to verify a store’s type).
requirements: No arguments; may be called at any time after the xmlsec-OpenSSL crypto is initialized (exact initialization requirements unknown).
Returned id is intended to be passed to xmlSec key store creation/utilities that accept xmlSecKeyStoreId.
Thread-safety or lifetime constraints of the returned class id are unknown.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeysStoreAdoptKey
functions.description: Adds the given key to the specified OpenSSL keys store, transferring ownership to the store. Typical usage is to create or load a key (xmlSecKeyPtr) and then adopt it into a store created with xmlSecOpenSSLKeysStoreGetKlass.
requirements: store must be a valid, initialized key store created for the OpenSSL keys store class (e.g., via xmlSecKeyStoreCreate(xmlSecOpenSSLKeysStoreGetKlass())).
store must not be NULL.
key must be a valid, initialized xmlSecKeyPtr and must not be NULL.
On success, ownership of key is transferred to the store; the caller must not destroy or modify the key after adoption.
Function returns an int status (xmlsec convention: 0 on success, a negative value on error; exact values not documented here).
The store must be in a state that allows insertion of new keys (no explicit concurrency guarantees; external synchronization may be required if used across threads).

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeysStoreLoad
functions.signature: int xmlSecOpenSSLKeysStoreLoad(xmlSecKeyStorePtr store, const char *uri, xmlSecKeysMngrPtr keysMngr);
functions.description: Loads keys into the given OpenSSL keys store from the specified URI. Intended to populate a store from a file or other source identified by uri; keysMngr may be used for auxiliary lookups or formats, depending on the xmlsec/OpenSSL backend.
requirements: store must be a valid, initialized OpenSSL keys store (created with xmlSecOpenSSLKeysStoreGetKlass).
store must not be NULL.
uri must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string pointing to a valid location understood by the backend (exact accepted URI schemes and formats are unknown).
keysMngr must be a valid xmlSecKeysMngrPtr if required by the backend; whether NULL is permitted is unknown.
Function returns an int status (xmlsec convention: 0 on success, a negative value on error; exact values not documented here).
The store should be empty or in a state where loading additional keys is allowed (semantics for merging vs. replacing are unknown).
Caller is responsible for ensuring underlying I/O permissions and availability of the referenced uri.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeysStoreSave
functions.signature: int xmlSecOpenSSLKeysStoreSave(xmlSecKeyStorePtr store, const char *filename, xmlSecKeyDataType type);
functions.description: Saves keys from the given OpenSSL keys store to the specified file, filtering by key data type. Typical usage is to persist a subset or all keys from the store into a file.
requirements: store must be a valid, initialized OpenSSL keys store (created with xmlSecOpenSSLKeysStoreGetKlass).
store must not be NULL.
filename must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string specifying an output file path writable by the process.
type must be a valid xmlSecKeyDataType mask/enum indicating which keys to save; exact accepted values are defined by xmlsec (details not in this header).
Function returns an int status (xmlsec convention: 0 on success, a negative value on error; exact values not documented here).
Caller must ensure the destination path is writable and has sufficient space; file format and encoding specifics are backend-defined and not documented here.

functions.name: xmlSecCryptoGetFunctions_openssl
functions.description: Returns the OpenSSL-specific xmlsec-crypto function table (DL functions) to plug xmlsec with the OpenSSL backend. Typical usage: pass the returned pointer to xmlSecCryptoDLLoadLibrary or similar registration code.
requirements: No arguments.
Caller must use the returned pointer only with the xmlsec dynamic-crypto loader APIs compatible with xmlSecCryptoDLFunctionsPtr.
Return value may be NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLInit
functions.description: Initializes the xmlsec OpenSSL crypto engine. Call once before using any xmlsec-OpenSSL functions.
requirements: Must be called before other xmlsec OpenSSL functions.
Should be called exactly once per process (typical pattern); if called multiple times, caller must handle non-zero/zero return semantics as defined by the library.
Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error; caller must check the return code.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLShutdown
functions.description: Shuts down the xmlsec OpenSSL crypto engine and releases associated resources.
requirements: Should be called after xmlSecOpenSSLInit and after all xmlsec-OpenSSL operations are finished.
Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error; caller must check the return code.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeysMngrInit
functions.description: Initializes an xmlsec Keys Manager for use with the OpenSSL backend (registers OpenSSL-specific key data, stores, etc.).
requirements: mngr must be a valid, allocated xmlSecKeysMngrPtr.
Must be called before using the manager to load keys/certs in the OpenSSL backend.
Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error; caller must check the return code.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLGenerateRandom
functions.description: Fills the given xmlSecBuffer with cryptographically secure random bytes using OpenSSL.
requirements: buffer must be a valid xmlSecBufferPtr, initialized and writable.
size specifies the number of random bytes to generate; should be > 0.
On success returns 0; negative value on error. Caller must check return code.
The buffer must have enough capacity or be growable; behavior follows xmlSecBuffer semantics (caller must handle errors if allocation fails).

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLSetDefaultTrustedCertsFolder
functions.description: Sets the default folder path where the OpenSSL/xmlsec backend looks for trusted certificates.
requirements: path must be a valid zero-terminated xmlChar* (UTF-8) string pointing to a directory path.
The directory should exist and be readable by the process (inferred).
Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error; caller must check the return code.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLGetDefaultTrustedCertsFolder
functions.description: Returns the default trusted certificates folder previously configured for the OpenSSL backend.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL if not set; caller must check for NULL before use.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; caller must not free it.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLSetLibCtx
functions.description: Registers an OpenSSL 3.x OSSL_LIB_CTX to be used by xmlsec-OpenSSL operations. Available only when XMLSEC_OPENSSL_API_300 is enabled.
requirements: Requires OpenSSL 3.x build with XMLSEC_OPENSSL_API_300 defined.
libctx must be a valid pointer to an initialized OSSL_LIB_CTX or NULL to reset (behavior inferred; check implementation).
Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error; caller must check the return code.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLGetLibCtx
functions.description: Returns the OpenSSL library context (OSSL_LIB_CTX) currently used by the xmlsec-OpenSSL backend. Available only when XMLSEC_OPENSSL_API_300 is enabled.
requirements: Requires OpenSSL 3.x build with XMLSEC_OPENSSL_API_300 defined.
May return NULL if no context is set; caller must check for NULL.
The returned pointer is not owned by the caller; do not free it.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLCreateMemBio
functions.description: Creates and returns a new OpenSSL memory BIO suitable for I/O buffering in xmlsec operations.
requirements: No arguments.
Returns a BIO* or NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.
Caller owns the BIO and must free it with BIO_free/BIO_free_all when done.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLCreateMemBufBio
functions.signature: BIO* xmlSecOpenSSLCreateMemBufBio(const xmlSecByte* buf, xmlSecSize bufSize);
functions.description: Creates a read-only OpenSSL memory BIO backed by the provided buffer contents.
requirements: buf must point to a valid memory region of at least bufSize bytes (if bufSize > 0).
bufSize is the buffer length; can be 0 for an empty BIO.
Returns a BIO* or NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.
Caller owns the BIO and must free it with BIO_free/BIO_free_all when done.
The function does not take ownership of buf; the data must remain valid for the lifetime of the BIO (inferred for typical membuf BIOs).

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLCreateReadFileBio
functions.description: Creates an OpenSSL file BIO opened for reading from the specified filesystem path.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL, zero-terminated C string.
The file at path should exist and be readable; otherwise creation fails.
Returns a BIO* or NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.
Caller owns the BIO and must free it with BIO_free/BIO_free_all when done.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataAesGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the xmlsec key data class for AES symmetric keys (OpenSSL backend). Use to register or create AES key data objects.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataAesSet
functions.signature: int xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataAesSet(xmlSecKeyDataPtr data, const xmlSecByte* buf, xmlSecSize bufSize);
functions.description: Sets the raw AES key material into the provided AES key data object.
requirements: data must be a valid xmlSecKeyDataPtr created for AES (from xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataAesGetKlass).
buf must point to key bytes; bufSize is the key length in bytes.
bufSize should match a valid AES key size (16, 24, or 32 bytes) (inferred).
Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error; caller must check the return code.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformAes128CbcGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for AES-128-CBC encryption/decryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformAes192CbcGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for AES-192-CBC encryption/decryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformAes256CbcGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for AES-256-CBC encryption/decryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformAes128GcmGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for AES-128-GCM authenticated encryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformAes192GcmGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for AES-192-GCM authenticated encryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformAes256GcmGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformKWAes128GetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for AES-128 Key Wrap (RFC 3394) used in XML Encryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformKWAes192GetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for AES-192 Key Wrap (RFC 3394) used in XML Encryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformKWAes256GetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for AES-256 Key Wrap (RFC 3394) used in XML Encryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataConcatKdfGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the key data class for ConcatKDF input key material (IKM) used in key derivation.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataConcatKdfSet
functions.signature: int xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataConcatKdfSet(xmlSecKeyDataPtr data, const xmlSecByte* buf, xmlSecSize bufSize);
functions.description: Sets raw secret material for ConcatKDF into the provided key data object.
requirements: data must be a valid ConcatKDF key data object (from xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataConcatKdfGetKlass).
buf must point to secret bytes; bufSize is the length in bytes and should be > 0 (inferred).
Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error; caller must check the return code.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformConcatKdfGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for the ConcatKDF key derivation operation.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataDesGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the key data class for DES/3DES symmetric keys.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataDesSet
functions.signature: int xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataDesSet(xmlSecKeyDataPtr data, const xmlSecByte* buf, xmlSecSize bufSize);
functions.description: Sets raw DES/3DES key material into the provided DES key data object.
requirements: data must be a valid DES key data object (from xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataDesGetKlass).
buf must point to key bytes; bufSize should match valid DES/3DES key sizes (inferred, e.g., 8 or 24 bytes excluding/including parity depending on implementation).
Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error; caller must check the return code.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformDes3CbcGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for Triple-DES (3DES) CBC encryption/decryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLTransformKWDes3GetKlass
functions.description: Returns the transform class for Triple-DES Key Wrap used in XML Encryption.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataDsaGetKlass
functions.description: Returns the key data class for DSA keys.
requirements: No arguments.
May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataDsaAdoptEvp
functions.description: Adopts an existing OpenSSL EVP_PKEY (DSA) into the xmlsec DSA key data object (takes ownership).
requirements: data must be a valid DSA key data object (from xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataDsaGetKlass).
pKey must be a non-NULL EVP_PKEY that contains a DSA key (inferred).
Ownership transfer semantics apply (inferred for Adopt APIs); after success, caller should not free pKey directly.
Returns 0 on success and a negative value on error; caller must check the return code.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLKeyDataDsaGetEvp
functions.description: Retrieves the underlying OpenSSL EVP_PKEY from a DSA key data object.
requirements: data must be a valid DSA key data object.
Returns an EVP_PKEY* or NULL on error; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: xmlSecOpenSSLErrorsDefaultCallback
functions.signature: void xmlSecOpenSSLErrorsDefaultCallback(const char* file, int line, const char* func, const char* errorObject, const char* errorSubject, int reason, const char* msg);
functions.description: Default error reporting callback for xmlsec-OpenSSL. It formats and reports errors with source location and context. Typically registered with xmlsec error handling to log OpenSSL-related errors.
requirements: file should be the source filename or NULL (if unknown).
line should be the source line number.
func should be the function name or NULL (if unknown).
errorObject and errorSubject may be NULL or descriptive strings.
reason is an integer error code.
msg may be a formatted message string or NULL.
Caller should not assume the callback throws; it’s intended for logging/reporting.

import os
import random
import struct
import time

# Generator for inputs that are filenames to on-disk data the harness will create.
# The fuzz stubs expect FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to point to an existing file or directory.
# Our buffer should contain a plausible on-disk layout description that the runtime
# can mirror. We therefore emit a simple tar-like manifest the harness can unpack,
# but since we cannot rely on any I/O here, we instead return bytes that encode
# both content and filenames so the runner can materialize them. Common, valid
# XMLSec key/cert store scenarios are included:
# - Single PEM certificate file (.crt)
# - Private key in PEM (.key) possibly encrypted or unencrypted
# - PKCS#12 bundle (.p12)
# - Directory layout with multiple certs (.pem) suitable for add-certs-path
# - XML file parseable by xmlSecParseFile
# - Concatenated PEMs file accepted by some loaders
#
# We format as a simple custom archive:
# magic: 8 bytes: b"FZMANIF\0"
# entry_count: uint16
# For each entry:
#   name_len: uint16
#   name: bytes (UTF-8)
#   mode: uint8  (0=file, 1=dir)
#   content_len: uint32 (only for files; 0 for dirs)
#   content: bytes
# A final field designates which path to pass to the API (the root path to use):
#   root_index: uint16 (index of the entry to be used as the filename/dir argument)
#
# The harness is expected to create entries accordingly and feed the selected root path
# to the target function. Our job: produce realistic, valid file contents.

PEM_CERT = """-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----

f4tqj6c2bX6z8qQv4s2GgGLH0yqgqXQvQqQp5nA1bK8zYqf7sJQm3e0aY2QfHDPk

9mV8v1m1+2o4Jm0kJ7n2t0hYq9mE0bXz6j9vJ3u+f2pJqf1l2k4zEo8bYcKQ2k1j

"""

MIIEvQIBADANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAASCBKcwggSjAgEAAoIBAQDPlznmWJgNw3xS

# Minimal XML that libxml2 can parse
XML_SAMPLE = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

# Small PKCS#12-like blob (not real, but some loaders accept any path; others will fail and the stub bails).
# To still produce valid inputs for loaders that do accept .p12, we keep this optional and
# primarily target PEM/dir scenarios which are widely supported.
FAKE_P12 = b"\x30\x82\x03\x0a\x02\x01\x03\x30\x82\x02\xf0\x06\x09\x2a\x86\x48\x86\xf7\x0d\x01\x07\x02\xa0\x82\x02\xe1\x30\x82\x02\xdd" + b"\x00"*64

# Helper to create a hashed symlink-style filename for cert stores

def _rand_name(rng, ext=""):
    alpha = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
    base = "".join(rng.choice(alpha) for _ in range(rng.randint(8,16)))
    return base + ext


def _emit_entry(name: str, is_dir: bool, content: bytes) -> bytes:
    name_b = name.encode("utf-8")
    mode = 1 if is_dir else 0
    if is_dir:
        content_len = 0
        payload = b""
    else:
        content_len = len(content)
        payload = content
    return struct.pack(
        ">H", len(name_b)
    ) + name_b + struct.pack(
        ">B", mode
    ) + struct.pack(
        ">I", content_len
    ) + payload


def _pem_concat(*parts: str) -> bytes:
    return ("\n".join(p.strip() for p in parts if p)).encode("utf-8") + b"\n"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    entries = []  # (name, is_dir, content)

    # Choose a scenario to maximize coverage of stubs needing directories and files
    scenario = rng.choice([
        "simple_pem_pair",        # directory with cert.pem and key.pem
        "certs_path_dir",         # directory with multiple .crt/.pem
        "pkcs12_file",            # single .p12 file
        "xml_doc",                # a parseable XML file
        "concat_pem_file",        # a file with concatenated PEMs
    ])

    root_index = 0

    if scenario == "simple_pem_pair":
        root_dir = _rand_name(rng)
        entries.append((root_dir, True, b""))
        entries.append((f"{root_dir}/cert.pem", False, PEM_CERT.encode("utf-8")))
        entries.append((f"{root_dir}/key.pem", False, PEM_KEY.encode("utf-8")))
        # Also add a bundle.pem to exercise loaders that can read a single file
        bundle = _pem_concat(PEM_CERT, PEM_KEY)
        entries.append((f"{root_dir}/bundle.pem", False, bundle))
        root_index = 0  # point to directory

    elif scenario == "certs_path_dir":
        root_dir = _rand_name(rng)
        entries.append((root_dir, True, b""))
        # Create several certificates with various extensions
        for i in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
            ext = rng.choice([".crt", ".pem"])
            name = _rand_name(rng, ext)
            entries.append((f"{root_dir}/{name}", False, PEM_CERT.encode("utf-8")))
        # Optionally include subdir with more certs
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            sub = f"{root_dir}/ca"
            entries.append((sub, True, b""))
            for i in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
                entries.append((f"{sub}/{_rand_name(rng, '.pem')}", False, PEM_CERT.encode("utf-8")))
        root_index = 0

    elif scenario == "pkcs12_file":
        filename = _rand_name(rng, ".p12")
        entries.append((filename, False, FAKE_P12))
        root_index = 0

    elif scenario == "xml_doc":
        filename = _rand_name(rng, ".xml")
        entries.append((filename, False, XML_SAMPLE.encode("utf-8")))
        root_index = 0

    elif scenario == "concat_pem_file":
        filename = _rand_name(rng, ".pem")
        concat = _pem_concat(PEM_CERT, PEM_CERT, PEM_KEY)
        entries.append((filename, False, concat))
        root_index = 0

    # Additionally, prepare a generic file for xmlSecBufferReadFile paths
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        data_dir = _rand_name(rng)
        entries.append((data_dir, True, b""))
        # a binary file with random bytes
        bin_name = f"{data_dir}/{_rand_name(rng, '.bin')}"
        rand_bytes = rng.randbytes(rng.randint(64, 512)) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randint(64,512)))
        entries.append((bin_name, False, rand_bytes))
        # small PEM cert to be read as data as well
        entries.append((f"{data_dir}/data.pem", False, PEM_CERT.encode('utf-8')))
        # Do not change root_index; extra resources are optional for the harness

    # Serialize manifest
    out = bytearray()
    out += b"FZMANIF\x00"
    out += struct.pack(">H", len(entries))
    for name, is_dir, content in entries:
        out += _emit_entry(name, is_dir, content)
    out += struct.pack(">H", root_index)

    # Ensure size limit
    return bytes(out[:4096])

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: output filename
# The fuzz stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to obtain a writable path for output
# such as debug dumps or saved key stores. Our generator must return a bytes
# buffer that the harness interprets as a filename. We will produce short,
# valid, writable-looking relative paths with directories that are likely to
# exist or be creatable by the harness (many harnesses write into a temp
# directory or current working directory). We avoid special characters and
# keep size small. We also vary extensions to trigger different code paths
# (e.g., .xml, .pem, .der, .p12) even if the callee may ignore them.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
EXTS = [
    "xml", "txt", "log", "pem", "der", "p12", "bin", "dat",
]
SUBDIRS = [
    ".",  # current directory
    "out",
    "tmp",
    "keys",
    "dump",
]
BASENAMES = [
    "keys", "store", "dump", "debug", "encctx", "keydata", "ids",
    "mngr", "openssl", "xmlsec",
]

def _rand_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose a basename + optional random suffix to diversify
    base = r.choice(BASENAMES)
    # ensure at least 1 random segment for broader coverage
    suffix_len = r.randint(0, 6)
    if suffix_len:
        rand_part = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(suffix_len))
        base = f"{base}_{rand_part}"
    ext = r.choice(EXTS)
    return f"{base}.{ext}"

def _rand_subpath(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose 1-3 levels with bias towards a single level
    levels = 1 if r.random() < 0.7 else r.randint(2, 3)
    parts: List[str] = [r.choice(SUBDIRS) for _ in range(levels - 1)]
    parts.append(_rand_name(r))
    # Join with forward slashes to be portable; many harnesses normalize
    return "/".join(parts)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Occasionally produce absolute-like paths for Unix/Windows, but prefer
    # relative to avoid permission issues. We only emit relative by default.
    path = _rand_subpath(r)

    # Keep under 256 bytes; the harness limit is 4096 overall
    if len(path) > 255:
        path = path[:255]

    return path.encode("utf-8")

#

# - Generate realistic PEM encodings:
#   * Single certificate in PEM

#   * PEM with extra headers (Proc-Type, DEK-Info) though not required, but harmless
#   * Optionally include an X509 CRL PEM between certs (many loaders skip, some accept)
# - Generate DER encoding (ASN.1) — here we provide a small valid DER certificate blob.
#   For simplicity and high validity, embed a known small self-signed test certificate
#   in both PEM and DER forms.
# - Randomly pick one variant based on seed.
# - Ensure output size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# We avoid malformed data; we provide commonly accepted forms by OpenSSL parsers.
